holidays.name: National Aviation Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate all things that fly, from jumbo jets to paper airplanes. Pilots, plane nerds, and dreamers look to the skies and salute humanity's urge to leave the ground.
holidays.origin: President Franklin D. Roosevelt proclaimed it in 1939 in the United States. The date was chosen because it is the birthday of Orville Wright, born August 19, 1871.
holidays.funFact: Orville Wright piloted the first powered flight in 1903, and it lasted just 12 seconds and covered 120 feet, which is shorter than the wingspan of a Boeing 747.

holidays.name: World Photography Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of the art, craft, and science of photography. People around the world share their favorite shots, and your camera roll full of 400 pictures of your lunch finally gets its moment.
holidays.origin: The date commemorates the 1839 announcement of the daguerreotype process by the French government, which gave the invention to the world free of charge. The day was promoted as a worldwide event in 2010 through an online gallery project.
holidays.funFact: The French government bought the daguerreotype patent and released it 'free to the world,' except in England, where Daguerre had already patented it.

holidays.name: National Soft Ice Cream Day
holidays.description: A salute to the swirly, melty, cone-topping goodness of soft serve. Expect to see dipped cones and rainbow sprinkles everywhere, plus a race to eat your treat before it drips down your arm.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday that reportedly honors the history of soft serve, which became popular in the United States in the 1930s and 1940s. Its invention is often credited to Tom Carvel, whose ice cream truck broke down in 1934 and forced him to sell his melting stock.
holidays.funFact: Tom Carvel's broken-down truck led to his discovery that customers loved the softer ice cream, and he went on to build the Carvel franchise.

holidays.name: International Orangutan Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate and protect the 'person of the forest,' the red-haired great apes of Borneo and Sumatra. It raises awareness of the threats these gentle, clever primates face.
holidays.origin: Established by the Orangutan Foundation International, which created it to highlight the endangered status of orangutans due to habitat loss from deforestation and palm oil production.
holidays.funFact: The word orangutan comes from the Malay phrase 'orang hutan,' meaning 'person of the forest,' and these apes build a fresh sleeping nest of leaves and branches nearly every night.

holidays.name: World Humanitarian Day
holidays.description: A day to honor aid workers who put themselves in harm's way to help others, and to inspire everyday people to do a little good in the world.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly designated it in 2008 to commemorate the 2003 bombing of the UN headquarters in Baghdad, which killed 22 people, including envoy Sergio Vieira de Mello.
holidays.funFact: The day's yearly campaigns often use the hashtag #ItTakesAVillage or similar slogans to highlight that anyone can be a humanitarian, and many people mark it by doing a random act of kindness.
